title: onprem-k8s-hop-by-hop-ops-playbook-phased-upgrade-notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an operational playbook + terraform module notes for performing phased Kubernetes control-plane and node upgrades in on-prem Redwood clusters (both vSphere VM-based clusters and bare‑metal PXE-boot fleets). Goal: run safe, observable, reversible upgrades with minimal disruption and clear rollback primitives.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Customer clusters may be either: stacked-etcd control plane on VMs (vSphere), or external/single-node etcd appliance (bare-metal installs).
- We control provisioning via Terraform modules (terraform/modules/cluster/*), but some sites use local image builders.
- Networking: calico/ipip overlay or Cilium depending on site; BGP underlay at some sites.
- KMS/HSM integration and audit logging must remain intact during upgrade.
- Desired canonical upgrade path example: Kubernetes 1.28.x -> 1.29.x (adjust to target minor versions based on security patches).

High-level strategy (phased rollout):
1) Pre-flight: telemetry + backups + plan generation.
2) Canary control plane (single CP node) on a spare rack or reserved VM set.
3) Canary worker nodes (small subset, multi-az/rack aware).
4) Gradual roll by rack/pool with health gates.
5) Post-upgrade validation and cleanup.

Pre-flight checklist (run at least 48–72 hours before a production rollout):
- Create an etcd snapshot and verify restore on an isolated host. Command snippet: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap-$(date +%F).db --endpoints=${ETCD_ENDPOINTS} --cacert=...
- Run terraform plan in a clone workspace to detect drift: terraform workspace select staging; terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars. Save plan artifact.
- Confirm backup of critical manifests (CRDs, network policies, RBAC) and export with kubectl get --all-namespaces -o yaml > /tmp/all-<date>.yaml
- Record current control-plane API latencies and error rates (Grafana dashboards: apiserver-latency, etcd-commit-duration, kubelet-restarts).
- Verify image registry reachability and pull credentials for kube-proxy, coredns, node-provisioner images.
- Open a rollback channel in Slack and create a Jira incident ticket (prefill with runbook steps).

Terraform module notes / gotchas (developer-facing):
- Module structure: terraform/modules/cluster -> control_plane.tf, workers.tf, bootstrap_templates.tf, vm_customization.tf. Keep control plane template immutable; use new template versions for upgrades (image_version variable).
- Avoid remote-exec for in-band cluster bootstrap where possible. Use cloud-init / guest customization to run kubeadm join commands; remote-exec causes timing flakiness during network disruptions.
- Vault integration: render per-node BMC credentials via external lookup and pass as sensitive variables using vault provider. Example: for_each = var.node_racks -> module.vm[each.key].bmc_user = lookup(var.bmc_creds, each.key)
- lifecycle "ignore_changes": only use for non-critical fields (tags, description). Do NOT ignore changes for disk, cpu, or network interface sets.
- Use image_template_version instead of hardcoding OS image IDs; maintain a content library for vSphere and an iPXE build tag for baremetal.
- When introducing a new kubelet cgroup driver or node OS kernel, add a per-node taint and a preparatory phase (see phased-prep below).

Phased preparatory changes (2-step):
- Phase A: Non-disruptive config updates (CNI config tweaks, kube-proxy mode change to ipvs) applied to one canary pool and validated for 24–48hrs.
- Phase B: Control-plane kube-apiserver/kube-controller-manager rollout to canary node(s).

Canary plan (control plane):
- Reserve 1 control-plane VM/host as canary. If vSphere: clone a template with new control-plane image version and attach to isolated portgroup. If baremetal: provision a spare blade with same hardware profile via PXE with target kubeadm config.
- Bootstrap control plane: kubeadm init --config canary-init.yaml (ensure certificate SANs cover external LB if used).
- Re-register core control plane components with a different label: node-role.kubernetes.io/upgrade-canary=true
- Smoke tests: kubectl get cs, run control plane sanity e2e subset (apiserver queries, create/delete namespace, coredns lookups).
- Monitor: etcd commit latency < 100ms, apiserver p95 latency < baseline*1.5, no spike in API 5xx. If any gate fails, destroy canary and iterate.

Worker canary plan:
- Pick 2–3 workers across 2 different racks/availability sets. Mark with label upgrade-canary=true. Drain one at a time: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force (use force only for dev/testing).
- Apply node-level kubelet/kube-proxy image changes via daemonset or kubeadm upgrade node. For setups using machine-image replacement, use terraform to spin new workers and remove old ones via scale down.
- Post-join validation: node Ready status, kubelet logs for < 1 minute of restarts, workloads reschedule success, no heapster/memory OOMs.

Full roll strategy by rack/pool (safety gates):
- Gate = all control-plane endpoints healthy, < 3% API 5xx over 10m, etcd leader election frequency unchanged.
- Roll order: workers in pool -> control-plane nodes (if stacked etcd do control-plane last after workers in same rack are updated to avoid quorum loss) -> API loadbalancer config update.
- Pause window: 30–60 minutes between racks unless metrics show green; extended to 2–4 hours if statefulset rollouts lag.

Rollback primitives:
- Control-plane rollback: if control plane shows persistent 5xx or etcd anomalies, restore etcd snapshot to cold standby and rejoin nodes. Keep previous VM/template image available and ability to reprovision old control-plane VMs via terraform apply -var image_version=<old>.
- Worker rollback: cordon and reprovision node with previous image or scale up prior machine set and drain replaced node.

Validation checklist (post-upgrade):
- kubectl get cs, kubectl get node (all Ready for > 10 minutes)
- No new CrashLoopBackOffs for system pods in last 30 minutes
- Network policy enforcement spot-check: e2e traffic tests across namespaces (use test harness scripts)
- Slack alerting: ensure no pagerflaps for 2h after upgrade window
- Run full suite of regression evals for critical customer prompts (small-run) to confirm model-serving infra unaffected (if customer uses dedicated infra).

vSphere-specific notes:
- Use VMware Content Library templates to manage OVA/VM templates. Always increment template version and push to site content library.
- Set VM hardware compatibility to 15+ and set vmxnet3 for network interface; use paravirtual SCSI for high IOPS nodes.
- When changing VM templates, preserve the vSphere annotations used by our inventory scripts (tag: redwood:cluster=<name>).
- For in-place upgrades of control-plane VMs: snapshot before power-cycle but prefer ephemeral templated replacement to prevent drift.

Bare-metal specifics:
- IPMI / BMC creds should be stored in Vault; use the BMC module to populate provisioning tool (e.g., Metal³ or Ironic) secrets.
- iPXE chain: use minimal initramfs with kernel parameters to mount root from overlay; ensure init scripts log to serial for debugging.
- For airgapped sites, mirror container images in local registry and update imagePullSecrets in kube-system namespace prior to upgrade.

Observability & SLO checks to automate pre/post gating:
- apiserver_request_duration_seconds:p95
- etcd_disk_backend_commit_duration_seconds:p99
- kubelet_runtime_operations_duration_seconds
- controlplane_pod_restarts (per 10m window)
- Prometheus alert: Increased API 5xx rate -> block next rollout step.

Post-mortem template (if rollback or incident):
- Summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations applied, follow-ups (owner + ETA), Terraform PRs reverted, Confluence link.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Decide whether to prefer image-based reprovisioning vs in-place kubeadm upgrades for all sites (tradeoff: predictability vs faster iteration).
- Add a terraform k8s-drift-detection job that runs nightly and posts plan diffs to a private S3/artifact store.
- Add a scripted canary test harness that runs lightweight surfacing tests automatically after each node or cp change.

Quick commands & snippets (reference):
- kubectl cordon <node>
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- kubeadm upgrade plan --kubernetes-version v1.29.0
- terraform plan -out=tfplan -var-file=site.tfvars && terraform show -json tfplan | jq '.'
- etcd snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/snap.db --endpoints=${ETCD_ENDPOINTS} --cacert=...

Notes: this is an iteration of existing bootstrap/upgrade docs but intentionally focuses on a hop-by-hop phased approach, terraform module cautions, and combined vSphere + baremetal operational guidance. Keep this doc lightweight and link to the canonical site-specific checklists in Confluence.

Owner + contact: Ava Chen (eng-private-deployments) — ping in #eng-private-deploys or @ava.chen for scheduling, or oncall via PagerDuty if an upgrade window triggers PD.
